changes.headline: Trump rejected Iran's 7-day Hormuz plan
changes.dek: Deal dead after Friday's close. The offer (via Qatar at UNGA): cease hostilities, reopen Hormuz within seven days, restart nuclear talks — in exchange for lifting the US naval blockade, releasing ~$12B in frozen assets, easing oil-export sanctions. Trump Saturday: 'They made a proposal, but I rejected it' — 'they're losing so badly.' Wall Street Journal: privately skeptical of any ceasefire; expects US bombing to resume after the November midterms. Sunday: FM Araghchi says Iran won't soften conditions; the US naval blockade stays 'in full force.'
changes.balance_read: Friday's −2% de-escalation fade is the reversal risk — the premium re-embeds on the reopen.

changes.headline: Gulf tanker volumes doubled in under a month
changes.dek: ~13.5 MMb/d clearing Hormuz. Tanker Trackers: Persian Gulf oil volumes have doubled in under a month as US forces now escort daytime transits (mines cleared from the main corridor). Kpler via Reuters: ~18 transits/day 10-day average; 33.7 MMbbl flowed out in the week starting Sep 20, roughly on par with the prior week. Javier Blas (Bloomberg Opinion): hiring a very large crude carrier runs $1M+/day, freight from inside Hormuz to Asia exceeds $22/bbl vs ~$2 a year ago.
changes.balance_read: ~13.5 MMb/d clearing the strait — near the July ceasefire peak — but the paper-vs-physical wedge (VLCC $1M+/day, Hormuz→Asia freight >$22/bbl) keeps the flat-price premium embedded.
changes.publishers: Tanker Trackers / Commodity Context / Javier Blas

changes.headline: Positioning: WTI crowded long, Brent washed
changes.dek: WTI length at 96th percentile; Brent specs −23% in a week. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) managed-money futures-only net long +101,828 (−4,451 w/w) — ~96th percentile of its 56-week range: crowded long by historical standards. Brent managed money (futures+options) net long +218,114 (−64,543 w/w) — specs cut ~23% of length in one week; the Brent crowded trade just washed.
changes.balance_read: Catch-up risk: WTI length is the lagging overhang — fresh escalation squeezes WTI hardest off the $11.91 spread.
changes.vintage: Data as of Tue Sep 22, released Fri Sep 25

changes.headline: Joliet partial restart only
changes.dek: ~275 kb/d still offline. Several units at the ~275 kb/d Illinois refinery returned Wednesday (Quantum Commodity Intelligence, Sep 24) — but Exxon has issued no public restart date and no confirmation of normal service. Offline = Western Canadian Select (WCS) wider and weaker; a confirmed full restart = the snap tighter for Nov/Dec.
changes.balance_read: ~275 kb/d of WCS demand still offline — the diff stays pressured until full rates.

changes.headline: Horizon ~day 20 of 35; record distillate cracks
changes.dek: ~300 kb/d SCO offline; gasoil crack record ~$95/bbl. Back ~mid-October (~day 20 of 35). Horizon essentially fully offline — roughly 300 kb/d of synthetic crude out. Second leg: the gasoil crack vs Brent printed a record ~$95/bbl (data back to 2011); NY Harbor ULSD crack ~$97 Friday after a record $113.48 Sep 16. Distillate-rich synthetic crude is the prime beneficiary. Cumulative Russian diesel destruction (Perm halted, Ilsky hit, Novoshakhtinsk suspended) adds more fuel.
changes.balance_read: ~300 kb/d of synthetic supply offline plus record distillate cracks — doubly supportive for SCO/WCS relative value.
changes.publishers: Heavy Reading maintenance calendar / ICE / RBN Energy

changes.headline: Egress functionally full; Mainline apportioned for October
changes.dek: ~272 kb/d spare (5.7%). Carry-forward June 2026 data: Keystone ~94%, Trans Mountain ~96%, Enbridge Mainline ~94% of available capacity. Spare takeaway down from ~310 kb/d in May. Oil Sands Magazine (Sep 22) puts Q4 basin production at a record 4.8 MMb/d. The Mainline is back into apportionment for October: light 7%, heavy 10% (Reuters, Sep 24).
changes.balance_read: Spare takeaway −38 kb/d m/m against record Q4 supply — widening-risk bias into winter.

changes.headline: Merey discounts deepen on war-risk freight
changes.dek: −$18/−$20 under Brent (freight-driven). Merey discounts deepened to −$18/−$20 under Brent (Sep 26 report, small outlet, unverified) vs −$14 to ICE Brent for October cargoes (Bloomberg, Sep 24). The widening is freight-driven — Aframax Jose→USGC $1.35M → $3.5M with war clauses — not demand-driven, so it could snap back if vessel availability improves.
changes.balance_read: While Jose→USGC freight holds at ~$7/bbl, Merey prices down to clear against WCS at Houston cokers — direct WCS widening pressure.

changes.headline: Brent–WTI blows out to 2026 wide
changes.dek: Brent–WTI ~$11.91, widest of 2026. Friday settles: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Nov26 $92.41 (−2.33%), Brent Nov26 $104.32 (−2.14%). WTI-specific drags: the surprise +2.969 MMbbl EIA build (vs ~0.64 draw expected), the November contract roll, and diesel-export-ban chatter pressuring US refiners' margins. Curve in steep backwardation — tight now, relief later.
changes.balance_read: WTI lost 7.9% on the week; Brent held the Hormuz premium. Framing per standing rule: this is the global balance, not Cushing.

flags.title: Sunday reopen gap risk
flags.detail: Trump rejected Iran's 7-day plan Saturday; Iran's FM won't soften conditions Sunday; the US naval blockade stays in full force. Friday's fade was the de-escalation trade — the deal died after the close. Trigger: Becomes a change if the electronic open gaps up on the rejection; killed by a flat or soft open.

flags.title: Joliet full-restart confirmation
flags.detail: Units returning = tightening in anticipation; a confirmed full restart = the snap tighter for Nov/Dec WCS. Trigger: Becomes a change if the company confirms full rates.

flags.title: Whiting talks Tue Sep 29
flags.detail: Sep 22 round ended with no deal; the refinery runs normally on contract workers. A walkout would idle a major PADD 2 heavy-crude buyer. Trigger: Becomes a change on a deal (status quo) or a strike call (PADD 2 demand offline).

flags.title: TMX toll decision
flags.detail: CER deadline Oct 1 for Jan 1, 2027 implementation (firm 80% → 90%). Trigger: Becomes a change on CER approval, denial, or delay.

flags.title: OPEC+ Oct 4 review
flags.detail: October quotas held; Iraq began shutting some field operations as storage fills — physical shut-ins spreading. Trigger: Becomes a change on any quota change or wider physical shut-ins.

flags.title: US diesel export ban decision
flags.detail: Trump endorsed a diesel export ban Sep 22 with a fast decision promised; current posture is voluntary refiner export cuts (no federal ban ordered). A ban traps barrels at home and crushes the record cracks supporting synthetic crude. Trigger: Federal ban announced → US distillate cracks fall, the record-crack leg of SCO support breaks; voluntary cuts only → softer easing.
flags.vintage: expires Administration plan expected early next week
